pull_request_lookup_failed.was: could not read merged pull requests; using ancestry alone
pull_request_lookup_failed.now: could not read merged pull requests (gh: simulated failure); using ancestry alone
pull_request_lookup_failed.why: The port names why the lookup failed, which the shell version never did. Carried over from tests/gh/test_output_parity.py's DIVERGENCES table unchanged: the reason now reaches the line from GhError rather than from the Python's gh_json, and reads the same.

lock_file_changed.why: pnpm only (ruling, 2026-09-20). The scenario's subject is a lock file the pull touched; the port watches one lock file, so the scenario builds that one. The reported line is unchanged, which is why the golden still applies.

lock_file_untouched.why: Same substitution. The state being asserted is a pull that did NOT touch the watched lock file, which needs the watched lock file to exist to mean anything.

notInTheTable.cannot list worktrees: tests/gh/test_output_parity.py records it: `git worktree list` failing left the shell version with an empty branch-to-worktree map, so it never printed a skip. The Python raises the skip the shell version meant to and the port keeps the Python's behaviour. There is no scenario for it in bash-output.json at all.

ghVocabulary.why: gh-sync-repo.py:263 to 290 spells six reasons a gh call could not be read. The port keeps three of them in the Python's words, 'gh is not on PATH' (off status 127), 'gh exited <n>' and 'gh returned rows that are not pull requests' (its own check on the rows), and reads the rest off GhError.detail, which is gh's own account without the 'gh <argv> failed: ' prefix the message carries, because lib/gh.ts owns that vocabulary now. Each line below is what the report says instead of what the Python said for the SAME state. They are recorded here rather than only in a test so that a change to the vocabulary has to be recorded to stay green; sync-repo.test.ts drives its example from this list, taking 'message' as the error the real client throws and 'account' as the part of it the report quotes.

lines.state: gh answered with something that is not JSON
lines.now: gh answered the merged pull requests with something that is not JSON: <parser message>
lines.account: gh answered the merged pull requests with something that is not JSON: unexpected token
lines.message: gh answered the merged pull requests with something that is not JSON: unexpected token

lines.state: gh answered with a payload that is not a list
lines.now: gh answered the merged pull requests with something that is not a list: <payload>
lines.account: gh answered the merged pull requests with something that is not a list: {"message":"Not Found"}
lines.message: gh answered the merged pull requests with something that is not a list: {"message":"Not Found"}

lines.state: gh is present and cannot be run
lines.account: cannot run gh: spawn gh EACCES
lines.message: gh pr list --state merged failed: cannot run gh: spawn gh EACCES

ghVocabulary.closed: Two lines left this table when lib/gh.ts gave GhError a detail field (layer 1). A refusal whose stderr is a SINGLE line, which is the usual shape ('gh: API rate limit exceeded'), used to reach the report with lib/gh.ts's whole message including the argv, because reasonFor took the last line of the message and the message was one line; it now reads as the Python's, gh's stderr last line alone. A gh that exited non-zero and said nothing used to read 'gh <argv> failed: gh exited <n>' and now reads 'gh exited <n>', which is the Python's own sentence. Neither is a divergence any more, so neither is listed above.

inProcessFanOut.why:
The fan-out is in-process (the design ruling in the approved plan), so a job has no exit status of its own, cannot be killed by a signal and cannot fail to start. It can still throw. gh-sync.py:123 to 135 folds a child that raised into THAT repository's section so the other sections survive; the port does the same with the line below, which replaces the three the child process took with it. The Python's first line carries the repository's basename (gh-sync.py:135 builds 'basename
  ✗ could not start the sync script: ...' as one string) because a child that never ran wrote no heading of its own; the port writes that same heading ahead of the line below whenever the job threw before its first line, so a section is never left sitting under the previous repository's name.
